title: AI Across the Listing Lifecycle
basis: Reconstructed on 2026-11-12 from the published index.md (paragraph for paragraph, in its own order) and spec.md (accepted 2026-10-21), which it replaces. Intent outcome, acceptance criteria AC-1 to AC-3, the thesis and the role are copied unchanged from the ai-in-listing-systems entry in journal-spec.json; the supporting claims, audience and AC-4 and AC-5 are this spec's own. Units added by this conversion: introduction roadmap p04; lead sentences that give the autonomy ladder (p08), the hosting table (p15), the five steps (p19), the evaluation table (p40), the trade-offs table (p46/p47) and the vertical table (p48/p49) their own units; the conclusion widened to two paragraphs (p59, p60).

know: Where generative AI and agents have shipped at marketplaces from 2023 to 2026 across the listing lifecycle (creation, search, moderation, pro tooling, valuation), and the autonomy ladder.

The control layer between models and listings (constrained generation, validation, provenance, trust checks before generation, the AI gateway and evaluation harness), conversational search as a query compiler, search as an API product for external agents, AI crawlers and data licensing, cost per outcome, evaluation, and the EU AI Act's dated obligations.
believe: A model's output is a proposal to be validated, never listing data.
The structured assets (taxonomy, attribute dictionary, search schema, trust rules) become more valuable when AI arrives, not less.
can_do: Review an AI proposal by asking what structured thing the model produces and what checks it.
Design an assisted insertion flow in which the platform validates every suggestion and records its provenance.
Register an AI use with its autonomy level, owner, evaluation set, cost per outcome, AI Act classification and kill switch.

audience.who: Group and brand Chief Architects, CPOs and CTOs, heads of data and ML, search and trust-and-safety leads deciding on AI features in 2026-2028. They know what LLMs are; they need the marketplace-specific architecture, evidence and governance.
already_knows: What an API, a database, an event stream, a search engine and Kubernetes are; what large language models are.

From earlier chapters: Veldmark (fictional), its brands and cast, Common Ground, Yardstick, the advice forum, Valuo and the Lyon apartment, Dealer Hub, the Keybridge neutrality decision; the taxonomy and bikes split, the attribute dictionary and attribute provenance; decision tiers, the gate tier and the model registry (ml-platform); DSA statements of reasons and the P2B Regulation; the failure patterns named in the chapter.
does_not_know: The terms this chapter owns: structured-output compiler, AI listing assistant, agentic search, agent-to-marketplace interface, autonomy level and ladder, AI gateway, AI use register.
MCP and its governance, faithfulness as a metric, the text-and-data-mining reservation, AI Act Article 50 and Annex III after the Digital Omnibus.
Veldmark's photo-to-listing pilot, its results and the February 2028 channel decision record.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Given an AI feature design that writes model output straight into listings, the reader names the controls the architecture lacks.
acceptance_criteria.probe: A marketplace launches an assistant that reads a seller's photos and writes the category, attributes, price and description straight into the listing, with the model choosing free-text values. Two weeks later its color filter has over a thousand distinct values, some prices are wrong, and fraud analysts say scam listings now read as well as genuine ones. Using only this chapter: what does the architecture lack, and what do you build?
acceptance_criteria.expected: A control layer in which the model proposes and the platform decides: screen photos against known scam images before generating; constrain the category to the taxonomy's current leaves and attribute values to the dictionary, returning 'unknown' rather than guessing; take the price range from a registered predictive model, never from the language model; draft text last with guardrails; require seller confirmation and record per-field provenance; shift fraud detection toward account, device, image and price signals; and register the use with an owner, evaluation set, cost per outcome and kill switch.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A reader of the opening alone (the callouts and the paragraphs before the first heading) can predict the chapter's sections.
acceptance_criteria.probe: After reading only the callouts and the paragraphs before the first heading: what will this chapter discuss, in what order, and with what kind of evidence?
acceptance_criteria.expected: AI as the translator between people and the marketplace's structures; where it has shipped across the listing lifecycle; the control layer that treats output as a proposal; the photo-to-listing assistant; search, external agents and crawlers; trust and safety, pro copilots and valuation; cost, evaluation and the EU AI Act; evidence from documented 2023–2026 marketplace launches, regulation and the fictional Veldmark's pilot.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A reverse outline of the chapter, written without the spec, lists the same controlling ideas in the same order as the post spec's sections and paragraphs.
Given a request to expose search to an external AI assistant, the reader states what the tools should return and the controls the channel needs.
acceptance_criteria.probe: A property portal is asked to let a popular AI assistant search its listings and send buyers' enquiries straight from the assistant. Using only this chapter: what should the portal offer, and on what terms?
acceptance_criteria.expected: Tools, not pages: search over the same index with a structured filter schema, public listing fields and tracked links back; no contact through the assistant, so messaging safety and attribution stay on the portal; per-partner quotas that protect the peak; leads attributed by channel and partner; the same organic ranking with paid placements labeled; a contract that forbids training on or long caching of returned listings; a decision record with a review date.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Given a marketplace's AI uses, the reader says which AI Act obligations apply and from when.
acceptance_criteria.probe: A marketplace group runs a conversational search assistant, generates listing descriptions, targets job ads with AI in its jobs section, and is asked to feed its valuation model into a bank's lending decisions. Using only this chapter: which EU AI Act obligations apply to which use, and from when?
acceptance_criteria.expected: Article 50 transparency for the conversational assistant and machine-readable marking of generated content from 2 August 2026 (marking for systems already on the market by 2 December 2026); job-ad targeting and candidate selection are high-risk under Annex III point 4 from 2 December 2027; a valuation feeding creditworthiness decisions on natural persons falls under Annex III point 5(b), also from 2 December 2027; whether the marketplace is a provider and whether seller-confirmed text is exempt are questions for counsel.

thesis.question: Where do AI and agents create value in listing marketplaces, and what architecture keeps them controlled?
thesis.claim: AI creates value in listing marketplaces where it translates people's intent into structures the marketplace already has (photos into a category and attributes, a sentence into search filters, a message into a policy label, a lead into a drafted reply). It stays controlled only behind a layer that treats every model output as a proposal: constrained to the taxonomy, the attribute dictionary and the search filter schema, validated and stored with per-field provenance, preceded by trust checks, and never the source of a number a buyer relies on, which comes from a registered predictive model. Search offered to external assistants becomes an API product with contracts, quotas and lead attribution, and every AI use is registered with its autonomy level, owner, evaluation set, cost per outcome, AI Act classification and kill switch.
thesis.disputed_by: The view that generative models make structured listing data less necessary, so a model can write free-text listings and answer buyers directly; or the practice of letting each team launch AI features from vendor demos, judged by uptake, with governance added after launch.
thesis.so_what: A Chief Architect who accepts this extends the model registry into an AI use register and blocks launches that cannot fill it in; treats the taxonomy, attribute service, search API and trust platform as the AI strategy; runs one AI gateway and evaluation harness for the group while brand teams build the features; puts each brand's channel strategy toward external assistants in a decision record with a review date; enforces data-use rules in pipelines; and approves AI features by cost per outcome.
thesis.how_why: Veldmark's photo-to-listing pilot (approved 15 November 2027, 5% of Tradeyard Netherlands' private sellers, goods only) was possible only because the group taxonomy and attribute service went live in October and the shared trust-and-safety platform in November. In nine weeks it produced about 154,000 assisted listings: 62% uptake, 92.4% of categories accepted unchanged, 78% of attribute suggestions accepted, unsupported claims in 1.9% of audited descriptions, median insertion time 2 min 50 s against 6 min 40 s, and 9 percentage points more started listings published, at €0.0062 of model cost per listing. Constrained values raised the share of cargo-bike listings recording electric assist from 61% to 88%; an earlier prototype with free-text attributes produced 1,100 distinct colors in two weeks. Fraudsters used the assistant as often as anyone, removing poor text as a scam signal. The search platform's head asked who pays for an external assistant's queries at the Sunday-evening peak of 31,000 queries per second, which is why search offered to assistants needs contracts and quotas.

supporting_claims.claim: AI creates value in listing systems where it translates people's intent into structures the marketplace already has, and every documented 2023-2026 implementation keeps the structured system of record and lets the model translate into it.

Every model output is a proposal: a control layer (gateway, prompt registry, tools, evaluation harness, validators and guardrails) constrains it to the taxonomy, attribute dictionary and filter schema, records per-field provenance, and never lets a model write to a system of record.

In an assisted insertion flow, trust checks run before generation, the price comes from a registered predictive model and never from the language model, and the seller confirms; constrained values improve the catalog, while fraudsters lose polished text as a signal against them.

Conversational search compiles a sentence into the existing filter schema, and search offered to external assistants becomes an API product with contracts, quotas, lead attribution and data-use terms, alongside a crawler and licensing policy for the involuntary channel.

The same propose-and-validate discipline governs moderation, pro copilots and valuation explanations: LLMs in the gray zone over a deterministic floor, copilots acting only with confirmation on permitted data, explanations that narrate retrieved facts only.

Every AI use is governed by its autonomy level, cost per outcome, evaluation and AI Act classification, recorded in an AI use register with an owner and a kill switch, and the structured assets are the AI strategy.

role.contribution: Extends model governance to generative AI and agents: AI proposes, the structured systems the earlier parts built decide, and every AI use is registered and costed.

additional_patterns.applies_to: scene to veldmark: the question, the vocabulary, the public evidence, the design, the worked example
trust to copilots: the other stages of the listing lifecycle, moderation first because the pilot's fraud finding leads into it, then buyer search and the channel, then pro tooling and valuation

flow.rationale: The scene poses Ingrid's question; the concepts give the terms every later section uses; the public evidence shows the pattern the control layer then designs for; the photo-to-listing pilot applies the layer to creation, the stage with the most evidence, and comes before the other stages because each of them reuses its parts (screening, constrained output, registered models). Trust and safety follows the pilot because the pilot's fraud finding is its question; search and the channel, then copilots and valuation, reuse the same pattern on other users. Cost, evaluation and the AI Act come after the features they govern, because they measure and classify those features, and their results are the fields of the AI use register the Chief Architect's view proposes; trade-offs, vertical differences, failure modes, the Chief Architect's view and the questions test and govern the whole. The architecture before the evidence would design for a pattern the reader has not seen; the pilot after search would show the compiler in its less documented use first; the register before the features would list fields with nothing to fill them.

sections.heading: Concepts: Generative AI, Agents and Autonomy
sections.controlling_idea: The chapter needs precise terms for generative AI, the structured-output compiler, agentic search, agent interfaces, autonomy and governance, and an autonomy ladder that ties each level to its controls.

advances_thesis.how: Defines the vocabulary, including the structured-output compiler and the autonomy ladder used to govern AI uses.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Seven terms carry the chapter, chief among them the structured-output compiler, in which a model translates unstructured input into a structure the marketplace already has and the structure is validated deterministically.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Autonomy levels form a ladder (suggest, draft, act with confirmation, act autonomously) in which each step up removes a person from the decision and needs stronger controls.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The author's rule is that anything that changes what buyers see about a seller's listing stays at draft or below unless the seller opts in, and anything that restricts users' rights follows the DSA's rules for automated decisions.

sections.heading: Where AI Has Shipped: The Lifecycle in Public Evidence
sections.controlling_idea: Documented marketplace launches from 2023 to 2026 cover every stage of the listing lifecycle and show three patterns: the structured system of record stays, rollouts are staged by structure, and the biggest 2026 change is distribution.

advances_thesis.how: Shows from public evidence that the model translates into existing structures.

transition_in.introduces: Where such features have actually shipped.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Between 2023 and 2026 marketplaces shipped AI at every stage of the listing lifecycle, mostly documented by company announcements, with trade press and third-party summaries labeled.

evidence.what: Lifecycle table: eBay magical listing (September 2023); Kleinanzeigen photo-to-listing (November 2025, trade press); OLX Auto Description (August 2026; 98% style and relevance, 89% faithfulness); OLX job-role extraction (January 2024; about 4,000 requests a day, 'approximately 15K per month'); coches.net filter compilation (November 2024; about 20,000 calls a day for about €19); leboncoin conversational assistant (March 2024); OLX Magic (2024, third-party summary; 5-10 s against 300-500 ms); OLX CompassGPT and AutoGPT in ChatGPT (February and April 2026); ImmoScout24 MCP server and ChatGPT app (January and March 2026); OLX Chat Images GenAI (January 2026); OLX AutoIQ (February 2026); Adevinta SEO (June 2023).
evidence.shows: Gives dated, sourced evidence for each stage, with what each case shows in its last column.
evidence.source: Company and trade sources as cited in the chapter

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Three patterns run through the table: every implementation keeps the structured system of record, rollouts are staged by structure, and the biggest 2026 change is distribution rather than modeling.

transition_in.introduces: The three patterns it shows.

sections.heading: Architecture: The Control Layer Between Models and Listings
sections.controlling_idea: Keeping the structured systems in charge takes a control layer of gateway, prompt registry, tools and evaluation harness with validators and guardrails, and hard boundaries between model output and listing data.

advances_thesis.how: Specifies the control layer that makes every output a proposal.

flow.rationale: Components first, then the checks around them, then the boundaries they enforce; the boundaries before the components would name rules with nothing to enforce them.

transition_in.carries_over: The pattern that every implementation keeps the structured system of record.
transition_in.introduces: The control layer that enforces it.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: An AI feature in a listing system needs four parts that the predictive-ML platform lacks: an AI gateway, a prompt and configuration registry, tools over the marketplace's own capabilities and an evaluation harness.

Validators check every output deterministically against the attribute dictionary, filter schema or policy taxonomy, and guardrails block contact details, payment instructions, prohibited items and unsupported claims, so models never write to systems of record directly.

evidence.what: Figure 2: models never write to systems of record directly.
evidence.shows: Shows the path every output takes through validator and guardrail into the same tools and contracts the rest of the platform uses.

transition_in.introduces: The validators and guardrails around them.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Four boundaries matter: model output is never a listing field until a validator and a person accept it, every field carries provenance, the search index stays the retrieval layer, and trust and safety runs on assisted content too.

evidence.what: Provenance values ai_suggested, seller_confirmed and seller_edited; the seller is responsible for a confirmed description, the marketplace for one it published unconfirmed.
evidence.shows: Shows why provenance matters for search, trust, analytics and liability.

transition_in.introduces: The boundaries they enforce.

sections.heading: Veldmark Worked Example: The Photo-to-Listing Assistant
sections.controlling_idea: Tradeyard's photo-to-listing assistant, built on the taxonomy service and the trust platform, screens photos first, constrains category and attributes, takes price from a registered model and drafts text last, and its pilot shows constrained AI improves the catalog while removing a weak fraud signal.

advances_thesis.how: Works the assisted insertion flow end to end with numbers.

flow.rationale: Approval, dependencies, design, one listing, the pilot's results, the design changes and rollout, then fraud: the order in which the pilot unfolded, so each result is read against the design that produced it.

transition_in.carries_over: The control layer and its boundaries.
transition_in.introduces: The control layer in one Veldmark assistant.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Tradeyard's assistant was approved for a narrow pilot on 15 November 2027, excluding vehicles, property, jobs and services because those need data that photos do not give.

evidence.what: Tradeyard Netherlands, iOS first, goods only, 5% of private sellers; exclusions follow eBay and Kleinanzeigen.
evidence.shows: Shows the staging-by-structure pattern applied.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The assistant depends on two Common Ground capabilities that went live just before it, the group taxonomy and attribute service (October 2027) and the shared trust-and-safety platform (November 2027), without which the model would have nothing to compile into and nothing to check it.

evidence.what: Taxonomy and attribute service, October 2027; shared T&S platform for Tradeyard NL and BE, November 2027.
evidence.shows: Shows the dependency of AI on structured assets.

transition_in.introduces: What made it possible.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Before the seller sees anything the assistant runs five steps: screen photos, propose a category from allowed leaves, propose attributes from the schema with 'unknown' allowed, take a price range from the registered price-hint model, and draft title and description last behind guardrails.

evidence.what: Perceptual hashes and an image classifier; a vision-language model ranking leaf categories; dictionary-constrained attributes; Tradeyard's price-hint model; guardrails stripping contact details, URLs, payment instructions and unsupported claims.
evidence.shows: Each step keeps the model inside a structure or a check.

transition_in.introduces: The steps built on them.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The seller confirms all five as an editable form, and the published listing carries an AI label and per-field provenance.

evidence.what: Figure 3: the language model ranks categories from an allowed list, fills a schema and writes prose last.
evidence.shows: Summarizes the five steps and where the price comes from.

transition_in.introduces: The seller's confirmation and the label.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: One Utrecht cargo bike shows the flow: no hash match, Bikes › Cargo at 0.94, seven of nine attributes with two returned as unknown, a €1,450-€1,700 price hint, and publication 2 minutes 10 seconds after the first photo.

evidence.what: Monday 6 December 2027, 19:05 CET; listed at €1,600; published 19:07.
evidence.shows: Shows each step on one listing.

transition_in.introduces: One listing through it.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: After nine weeks the pilot produced about 154,000 assisted listings with high uptake and acceptance, faster insertion, more published listings and a model cost below one cent per listing.

evidence.what: Pilot measures to 17 January 2028: 62% uptake; 92.4% category accepted; attributes 78/15/7%; 1.9% unsupported claims in a 2,000-listing audit; 2 min 50 s against 6 min 40 s; +9 points started-to-published; +4% contacts (weak signal); €0.0062 per assisted listing.
evidence.shows: Measures the pilot, each with how it is measured.

transition_in.introduces: The pilot's results in January.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Two findings changed the design: constrained values raised attribute coverage, the Attribute Junkyard in reverse, and unsupported claims clustered in condition superlatives that the guardrail now strips.

evidence.what: Electric assist recorded on cargo bikes rose from 61% to 88%; an earlier free-text prototype produced 1,100 distinct colors in two weeks.
evidence.shows: Shows constraint, not the model, produced the gain.

evidence.what: Figure 4: junkyard against swatch cabinet.
evidence.shows: Pictures free-text against constrained values.

transition_in.introduces: What they changed in the design.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: At full rollout model cost is not the constraint; evaluation across four languages and 1,640 leaf categories is, so the forum extends the pilot only where evaluation sets exist.

evidence.what: About €230,000 a year forecast; extension to 25% of Netherlands sellers and Belgium on iOS and Android from 24 January 2028; Poland and Portugal once evaluation sets exist.
evidence.shows: Shows evaluation, not spend, gating the rollout.

transition_in.introduces: What limits the rollout.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Fraudsters used the assistant as often as anyone, so polished text stopped being a signal against them and the trust model must lean on account, device, image and price signals, with generated photos countered behaviorally rather than visually.

evidence.what: 2,300 attempts with matching photos blocked in the pilot; generated apartment photos have no hash to match.
evidence.shows: Shows what screening catches and what it cannot.

evidence.what: Figure 5: two equally polished listings, signals lighting for the fraudulent one.

sections.heading: AI in Trust and Safety
sections.controlling_idea: Generative models help moderation where policy changes faster than labels accumulate, under three rules: LLMs in the gray zone only, a deterministic floor, and respect for the law on automated decisions.

advances_thesis.how: Applies propose-and-validate to moderation.

transition_in.carries_over: The pilot's fraud finding: polished text no longer separates scams, and the trust model must lean on other signals.
transition_in.introduces: Where generative models themselves help moderation, and the rules that keep them controlled.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Three rules keep LLMs in moderation controlled: use them only in the gray zone, keep a deterministic floor, and respect the DSA's limits on automated decisions.

evidence.what: About 138,000 new-listing decisions a week go to human review at Tradeyard; 94% are decided automatically.
evidence.shows: Shows where LLM triage pays.

evidence.what: DSA Article 20(6): complaint decisions not taken 'solely on the basis of automated means'.
evidence.shows: Shows the legal limit.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: OLX's chat-image model shows a well-scoped gate-tier use, and Veldmark's gray-zone design follows the same scope discipline with every model registered.

evidence.what: OLX Chat Images GenAI (2026): one fraud vector, real time, measured precision.
evidence.shows: Shows narrow scope in the gate tier.

transition_in.introduces: A documented use that follows them.

sections.heading: Search, Agents and the New Channel
sections.controlling_idea: In search the model compiles a sentence into the existing filter schema, agentic flows belong only in high-consideration journeys, and search offered to external assistants and crawled by AI companies becomes a channel governed by contracts, quotas, attribution and a crawler policy.

advances_thesis.how: Applies the proposal pattern to search and the new distribution channel.

flow.rationale: Search on own surfaces first (compiler, its limits, agents), then the voluntary external channel, then the involuntary one; the crawler trade-off last because it needs both channels.

transition_in.carries_over: The propose-and-validate pattern in listing creation and moderation.
transition_in.introduces: The same compiler pattern in buyer search, then the new channel.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Hearthly's conversational search compiles a sentence into its existing filter schema, shows the filters to the user and runs normal search, which keeps results explainable and cost low.

evidence.what: The coches.net and leboncoin pattern.
evidence.shows: Shows the compiler pattern in documented use.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Natural language helps mainly where filters are many and vocabulary is vague, and a conversational layer that cannot say there is no filter for a wish will invent one.

evidence.what: 'Quiet', 'bright', 'near a good school' have no filter.
evidence.shows: Shows the limit of compilation.

transition_in.introduces: Where it helps and where it must refuse.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Agentic search costs an order of magnitude more latency, so it belongs in high-consideration journeys rather than default search.

evidence.what: OLX's account: 5-10 seconds against 300-500 ms; a blank chat interface replaced by the familiar search page with AI built in.
evidence.shows: Shows the cost and the interface lesson.

transition_in.introduces: Multi-step agentic search.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: When an external assistant calls the marketplace, search becomes an API product whose tools (search with a filter schema, listing summaries, links back) have their own release mechanics.

evidence.what: ImmoScout24's cached tool descriptors; Rightmove's FY2025 results (February 2026) on conversational search and a ChatGPT app.
evidence.shows: Shows assistants get tools, not the website.

evidence.what: Figure 6: an external assistant gets tools, not pages.
evidence.shows: Pictures the authenticated, rate-limited, tracked interface.

transition_in.carries_over: Search on the marketplace's own surfaces.
transition_in.introduces: Search called by other companies' assistants.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Veldmark's February 2028 decision record answers the questions every group faces about the channel: which brands first, what tools return, no contact through the assistant, quotas, attribution, ranking and partner data use.

evidence.what: Seven decisions with reasons: Hearthly France and Motorvane Germany first; public fields and a tracked link; no contact through the assistant; per-partner quotas lowered Sunday 20:00-22:00 CET; leads tagged by channel and partner; same organic ranking, paid labeled; no training or long caching by partners.
evidence.shows: Shows the channel governed as an API product.

transition_in.introduces: Veldmark's decisions for it.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The other half of the channel is involuntary: AI crawlers copy the inventory that is a marketplace's product and return no traffic.

transition_in.introduces: Crawlers that take data without asking.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The architecture has three levers against crawlers: technical controls, a machine-readable legal reservation, and commercial licensing.

evidence.what: Cloudflare blocked AI crawlers by default for new domains and announced pay-per-crawl on 1 July 2025; AI Act Article 53 and Article 4(3) of Directive (EU) 2019/790.
evidence.shows: Shows the infrastructure market and the law supporting the levers.

transition_in.introduces: The three levers.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Crawler policy trades data protection against search traffic, so the brand's GM decides it quarterly with SEO and legal and the architecture makes each lever a configuration.

evidence.what: 46% of Tradeyard's web sessions start from organic search.
evidence.shows: Shows what blocking could cost.

transition_in.introduces: The cost of using them.

sections.heading: Pro Copilots and Valuation Explanations
sections.controlling_idea: Copilots for pros act only with confirmation on the dealer's own and permitted data, and valuation explanations narrate retrieved facts under a validator that checks every number.

advances_thesis.how: Applies propose-and-validate to pro tooling and valuation.

transition_in.carries_over: Search and the channel, the buyer side of the lifecycle.
transition_in.introduces: Pro tooling and valuation.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Motorvane's dealer copilot acts with confirmation inside Dealer Hub, uses only the dealer's own and Motorvane's market data, explains prices in public price-rating terms, and Keybridge's equivalent stays inside Keybridge's tenancy.

evidence.what: Price change for forty cars after a preview; March 2027 Keybridge neutrality decision.
evidence.shows: Shows autonomy and data limits on a copilot.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Valuo explanations narrate structured inputs and may not introduce a comparable, number or trend, because an explanation that invents a comparable turns an estimate into a misrepresentation.

evidence.what: Lyon apartment: 68 m², Lyon 7e, energy class D, estimate €372,000-€401,000.
evidence.shows: Shows the retrieve-then-narrate pattern on the canonical case.

transition_in.introduces: Constraints on generated explanations.

sections.heading: Cost and Evaluation
sections.controlling_idea: Generative AI should be budgeted by cost per outcome, with volume moved to cheaper hosting as tasks stabilize, and guarded by evaluation at five stages, with faithfulness measured apart from fluency.

advances_thesis.how: Supplies the cost and evaluation fields of the register.

transition_in.introduces: What they cost and how they are evaluated.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Every feature is paid per call, which makes cost visible, but the public numbers are few and old.

evidence.what: coches.net ~20,000 calls a day for ~€19 (2024); OLX ~4,000 calls a day, 'approximately 15K per month' (2024); Veldmark €0.0062 per assisted listing (illustration).
evidence.shows: Gives the only public cost figures and Veldmark's.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The unit that matters is cost per outcome, reported by the gateway per feature and brand with a budget and an alert.

transition_in.introduces: The unit that outlasts them.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Cost per outcome also depends on where a model runs, and there are four options, from a frontier model through a provider API to a distilled classical model, each fitting a different volume and task stability.

evidence.what: Model choice and hosting: frontier API, small or mid-sized API, self-hosted open model, distilled classical model, with strengths, weaknesses and fits.
evidence.shows: Matches each hosting option to the tasks it fits.

transition_in.carries_over: Cost per outcome as the unit to manage.
transition_in.introduces: Where a model runs, the main lever on that cost.

advances_thesis.how: Gives the hosting lever on cost per outcome.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The documented trajectory matches the table, so the author's rule is to start with an API to learn the task and move volume down the table as it stabilizes, keeping the gateway so that the move is a routing change.

evidence.what: leboncoin moved guardrails from prompts into fine-tuning for latency; OLX's job-role extraction cost prompted evaluation of self-hosted models.
evidence.shows: Shows real teams moving down the table as tasks stabilized.

transition_in.introduces: Documented moves along it and the author's rule.

advances_thesis.how: Gives the rule for moving volume to cheaper hosting.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Evaluation runs at five stages, from golden sets before launch to sampled audits of production traffic.

evidence.what: Golden sets, regression on every change (block if category accuracy drops more than 1 point), adversarial testing, online experiments, sampled production audit.
evidence.shows: Shows each stage with a listing example.

transition_in.carries_over: Cost levers: the unit and where models run.
transition_in.introduces: The evaluation that must guard every change, including a move to a cheaper model.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Faithfulness deserves its own metric, because fluent and wrong is the characteristic failure of generative models and usage metrics miss it.

evidence.what: OLX Auto Description: 98% style, 89% faithfulness.
evidence.shows: Shows fluency and faithfulness diverging.

transition_in.introduces: The metric they must include.

flow.rationale: The cost figures, then the unit that outlasts them, then hosting as the lever on that unit, then evaluation, which guards every change including a move down the hosting table; evaluation before hosting would leave the cheaper-model move unguarded in the reader's mind.

sections.heading: Regulation: The EU AI Act for Marketplaces
sections.controlling_idea: The AI Act's dated obligations, after the Digital Omnibus, touch marketplaces through Article 50 transparency and Annex III high-risk uses in jobs and credit, and Veldmark designs so as not to depend on unresolved legal questions.

advances_thesis.how: Supplies the AI Act classification field of the register.

transition_in.introduces: Legal obligations as governance.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The AI Act applies in phases, some moved by the Digital Omnibus (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744), with five dated obligations relevant to marketplaces, stated as of the book's October 2026 research date and placed against the Veldmark story's November 2027 to February 2028 timeline, across which the 2 December 2027 high-risk date falls.

evidence.what: 2 February 2025; 2 August 2025; 2 August 2026 with marking by 2 December 2026; 2 December 2027; 2 August 2028.
evidence.shows: Gives each obligation's date and marketplace relevance.
evidence.source: European Parliament Legislative Train (September 2026); AI Act implementation timeline (August 2026)

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Annex III makes AI that targets job ads or selects candidates, and creditworthiness evaluation, high-risk, which reaches jobs marketplaces and valuation models feeding lenders. Lucía's answer (none of the six is high-risk as proposed) still holds after that date.

evidence.what: Annex III point 4(a): 'to place targeted job advertisements, to analyse and filter job applications, and to evaluate candidates'.
evidence.shows: Shows the scope in the Act's words.

transition_in.carries_over: The high-risk date in the table.
transition_in.introduces: Which marketplace uses it reaches.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Whether Article 50's marking duty applies to a marketplace assistant is a question for counsel, so Veldmark labels and marks assisted content from launch regardless.

transition_in.introduces: Article 50 and Veldmark's answer.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The AI Act sits alongside the DSA, the P2B Regulation, consumer law and the GDPR covered elsewhere in the book.

transition_in.introduces: The other rules that also apply.

sections.heading: Trade-offs
sections.controlling_idea: Each AI decision has a default and a condition under which the alternative is right, and the defaults keep model output in drafts and schemas.

advances_thesis.how: Gathers the chapter's decisions as choices with conditions.

transition_in.carries_over: The decisions made section by section.
transition_in.introduces: All of them side by side.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Each decision in the chapter has a default and a condition under which the alternative is right.

evidence.what: Seven decisions: where AI writes, output form, search interface, external channel, model hosting, crawler policy, moderation.
evidence.shows: Shows when each option is right.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The first two rows carry the chapter's argument: wherever output is searchable, filterable or seen by buyers, the model drafts into a schema and a person or validator decides.

transition_in.introduces: The rows that carry the argument.

sections.heading: Vertical Differences
sections.controlling_idea: How much each AI decision matters depends on the vertical: the assistant pays most in general classifieds, conversational search and the external channel in real estate and automotive, and jobs carries the highest AI Act exposure.

advances_thesis.how: Shows where the value and risk concentrate.

transition_in.introduces: How they differ by vertical.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: How much each decision matters depends on the vertical.

evidence.what: Assistant value, creation risk, conversational fit, external channel fit (ImmoScout24, OLX CompassGPT, OLX AutoGPT), copilots, AI Act exposure across four verticals.
evidence.shows: Compares the verticals on each dimension.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: General classifieds gain most from the assistant, real estate and automotive from conversational search and the external channel, and jobs carries the highest regulatory risk.

transition_in.introduces: What it adds up to.

sections.heading: Failure Modes
sections.controlling_idea: Each design choice has a characteristic failure, from free-text attributes to crawler policy by accident.

advances_thesis.how: Shows what breaks without each control.

transition_in.introduces: What goes wrong when choices are made badly or not at all.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Nine failure modes follow from missing controls: free-text attributes, an assistant that helps scammers, numbers from the language model, prompt changes without regression tests, agentic search as default, contact through the assistant, conversation data at the vendor, crawler policy by accident and AI-washed explanations.

sections.heading: The Chief Architect's View
sections.controlling_idea: A Chief Architect governs AI with an AI use register, treats the structured assets as the AI strategy, owns the gateway centrally, decides channel strategy per brand, enforces data-use rules in pipelines, budgets by outcome and watches a short list of indicators.

advances_thesis.how: Turns the chapter into group decisions.

transition_in.introduces: The group decisions that prevent them.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Extend the model register into an AI use register that every feature must fill in before launch.

evidence.shows: Shows reuse rather than a parallel register.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Make the structured assets the AI strategy, because AI features compile into them and the order of Common Ground's deliveries was the order of what AI could do.

transition_in.introduces: The assets AI depends on.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Own the gateway and evaluation harness centrally and the features locally.

transition_in.introduces: Who owns the shared AI platform.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Decide each brand's channel strategy explicitly in a decision record with a review date.

transition_in.introduces: The per-brand channel decision.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Write data-use rules down and enforce them in pipelines, including the Keybridge neutrality commitment.

transition_in.introduces: Data-use rules.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Budget AI by outcome and move stable volume to cheaper hosting.

transition_in.introduces: Budgets.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Watch a short list of indicators, from register coverage and faithfulness to crawler traffic and unclassified AI Act uses.

sections.heading: Questions to Ask
sections.controlling_idea: Ten questions let a reader review any AI feature against the chapter.

advances_thesis.how: Turns the chapter into a review checklist.

transition_in.introduces: Questions for a design review.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Ten review questions start from what structured output the model produces and what checks it, and cover provenance, trust, cost, evaluation, the external channel, crawlers, the AI Act and data use.

conclusion.heading: From AI to the Long View
conclusion.synthesis: AI is a translator between people and the structures the marketplace already has: where those structures are clean, the control layer lets AI make listing, search and pro work faster while every proposal stays checked, attributed and costed, on Veldmark's own surfaces or as tools for another company's assistant, and recorded in the register; where they are not, AI accelerates the mess.
conclusion.so_what: A Chief Architect's AI roadmap is therefore the structured-asset roadmap, and Ingrid's question decides every proposal.

callback.to: The opening's picture of sellers and buyers doing the work of translation, and Ingrid's question about the six requests.
callback.how: The reader now sees that translation is what AI takes over and that one question answered all six requests.

takeaway.content: Ask of every AI proposal what structured thing the model produces and what checks it, and invest in the structures it compiles into.

hand_off.carries_over: AI is safe where the marketplace's structures are clean and accelerates the mess where they are not, and it is only one stressor a platform must absorb.
hand_off.introduces: Keeping the platform coherent over a decade of stressors: acquisitions, regulation and the swing between central and local control.

transition_in.carries_over: The whole chapter and the review questions.
transition_in.introduces: The answer to Ingrid's question for all six requests.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Ingrid's question had the same answer for all six requests, because AI arrives as a translator into existing structures: where they are clean the control layer keeps every proposal checked, attributed, costed and registered, on own surfaces or another company's assistant; where they are not AI accelerates the mess, so the AI roadmap is the structured-asset roadmap.
AI is only one of the stressors a platform must absorb over a decade, alongside acquisitions, regulation and the swing between central and local control, which long-term-evolution takes up.

transition_in.introduces: The decade-long view in the next chapter.
